newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen rise seen topping out at 112.60/65.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen rise seen topping out at 112.60/65.

text.p: The dollar stabilized above support at 111.65 yen, following a sharp slide overnight, and technical analysts said further short-term gains up to resistance at 112.65 yen were likely before the downtrend resumes.

Dollar/yen pierced but failed to stay below strong support at 111.30 yen, July's highs, after remarks from a Japanese finance minister and a large U.S. manufacturing group put the greenback under pressure.

"We are probably in for a bit of ranging in dollar/yen. It could reach 112.60, maybe higher, but after that it will start heading lower again," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
"The important level is 113.00 to 113.10. If we get above there, we go to new highs," he added.
The dollar also slipped against the mark on renewed signs of vigor in the German economy, but the greenback bounced off support at 1.50 marks, analysts said.

"The direction on the dollar is down against the mark, but the fact that it bounced off of 1.50 (marks) shows it should produce a rally back above 1.52 to the upper support of 1.5280," said Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc.
Most analysts were negative for the dollar/mark near-term.

"If the (dollar/mark) is able to stay firm, that's pretty positive/ But there is a risk of the thing coming off and coming off pretty hard again from here -- meaning in the next 24 hours," Solin said.
Trendline support in sterling/mark was quoted at 2.4580 marks and Ascani said he thinks "there's a good chance" the market will fall back to that level.
Sterling/mark support was quoted at 2.4650 and 2.4530 marks with resistance at 2.4980 marks.
Mark/yen support at 73.89 held on Thursday with the next layer of support quoted at 73.42. Resistance lies at 74.37, 74.67, and 74.91 yen, analysts said.
